note: BeyClub's own editorial notes. These are our read on each part, not the Taiwanese or Japanese sources' opinion, and are shown in the app under a 'BeyClub notes' heading. Keyed by 'category:id'. Parts without an entry simply omit the section.

pros: The most successful blade in the tournament record by a wide margin
Outlasts almost anything in a stamina battle once it settles
Flexible — performs on several ratchet and bit combinations rather than one narrow build
cons: Vulnerable to a committed attack type that reaches it early
So common that opponents come prepared for it
blade:UX-03.technique: Launch flat and controlled rather than at maximum power — the goal is a clean, stable spin that survives the opening exchanges, not an aggressive first hit.

pros: Second only to Wizard Rod in recorded placements
Hits hard while still holding a respectable spin
Strong on the widely available 1-60 ratchet
cons: Gives up ground to pure stamina builds if the knockout doesn't land
blade:BX-23.technique: Commit to the attack early. Its win condition is a burst or knockout in the first few exchanges, so launch with pace and angle rather than playing for the long spin.

pros: Consistently one of the highest-placing attack blades
Pairs well with the E bit for an attack build that still finishes spins
cons: Left-spin, so it needs a left-spin launcher
Punished badly by a mistimed launch
blade:BX-34.technique: Left-spin gives it an advantage in opposite-spin matchups — use that deliberately rather than treating it as an ordinary attacker.

pros: Top-tier attack power, rated X by the Taiwanese community
Very strong opening hit
cons: Stamina is its weak point — the source itself flags this
blade:UX-15.technique: Aim to finish the match early. Combine with a ratchet that keeps it aggressive and accept that a long spin is not the plan.

pros: A proven attack blade with a deep tournament record
Well suited to burst finishes
cons: Loses out to modern stamina blades if the knockout doesn't land
blade:UX-01.technique: A pure aggression pick — launch hard and hunt for the burst.

pros: Balanced enough to handle a range of opponents
Rated highly by both the Taiwanese and Japanese communities
cons: Rarely the outright best answer to any single matchup
blade:UX-08.technique: A dependable all-rounder — a good pick when you don't know what you're facing.

pros: The single most successful bit in the tournament record
Gets into a rush attack faster than almost anything else
cons: Burns through spin quickly — a poor choice if the match goes long
bit:R.technique: Built for rush attacks. Launch with power and aim to end the match in the opening exchanges.

pros: Nearly matches R for placements while holding spin better
Very widely playable — appears across more combos than any other bit
cons: Neither the fastest attacker nor the longest spinner
bit:LR.technique: A safer rush option than R. Good default when you want attack pressure without throwing away the long game.

pros: Excellent balance of attack and stamina
One of the top three bits by recorded wins
cons: Rarely the extreme best at either job
bit:H.technique: The reliable middle ground — pick it when the matchup is unknown.

pros: Strong stamina retention
A core part of the top stamina builds
cons: Little attack threat — it wins by outlasting, not by hitting
bit:B.technique: Launch for stability. Let the opponent spend their energy attacking and take the spin-finish.

pros: High placement rate despite appearing in fewer combos
Holds spin well for its speed
cons: More specialised than the general-purpose bits
bit:E.technique: Best on blades that already have the weight to attack — it adds finishing spin rather than raw aggression.

pros: The most successful ratchet in the record
Low profile keeps the bey stable and hard to knock over
cons: Low height gives up some attack angle against taller opponents
ratchet:1-60.technique: The default competitive choice. If you're unsure which ratchet to run, start here.

pros: Nearly matches 1-60 for wins and appears in more distinct combos
Extra contact points help in exchanges
cons: Slightly heavier feel changes launch timing
ratchet:9-60.technique: A strong alternative to 1-60, especially on stamina builds where the extra contact helps survive hits.

pros: Third by wins and one of the most widely played
Good compromise between stability and weight
cons: Outperformed at the very top by 1-60 and 9-60
ratchet:3-60.technique: A solid, forgiving choice while you work out which extreme suits your blade.

pros: Well represented across successful attack builds
Suits blades that want a bit more mass low down
ratchet:5-60.technique: Pair it with attack blades that benefit from the added weight in the exchange.
